title: `viewFilterRuleToNode` passes an array value through verbatim on a SCALAR operator — a saved view's rule reaches the server as a node it refuses
body:
Filed by the `domain:ui` PM seat (`session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S`) on behalf of the objectui#8530 dev, which measured it while landing PR #8551 and was locked out of dedup (four `search_issues` refused by the rate limit; repo-scoped REST 403). ⛔ Not claimed.

## Measured

`packages/core/src/utils/filter-converter.ts:371-378`:

```ts
function viewFilterRuleToNode(rule: ViewFilterRuleLike): FilterNode {
  const operator = normalizeFilterOperator(rule.operator as string);
  return (
    rule.value === undefined
      ? [rule.field, operator]
      : [rule.field, operator, rule.value]
  ) as FilterNode;
}
```

`rule.value` is never inspected. So a stored view rule carrying an array on a **scalar** operator travels through unchanged:

```
toFilterNode([{ field: 'tags', operator: 'equals', value: ['a'] }])
  →  [['tags', 'equals', ['a']]]      isFilterAST: true
  →  parseFilterAST  →  { tags: ['a'] }        (measured, spec 17.3.0)
```

— which the server then refuses two layers away, exactly as objectui#8530 described for the object arm.

## Why it is its own card

objectui#8530 / PR #8551 added the array-comparand refusal to `convertFiltersToAST`'s **object** arm. This is the **stored-view** path, and that fix deliberately does not reach it: the two enter the lowering at different doors and only one of them was in scope.

The result is the asymmetry this repo keeps filing: a hand-authored `{ tags: ['a','b'] }` now fails fast with a message naming `$in`, while the same mistake **saved into a view** still travels silently to a 400 the author cannot attribute to their filter.

## Direction

The same ruling applies — **refuse, and name `$in`** — for the same reason PR #8551 gives: the ObjectQL AST has no array-equality node, so the lowered node can never select anything, and silently rewriting `equals` into `in` would change the author's meaning.

⚠️ But check the scalar/multi-value split first: `in` and `between` rules legitimately carry arrays through this same function, and the objectui#8530 dev verified that path never enters the object arm, so it has never been exercised against a refusal here. Whatever guard lands must key on the **operator's arity**, not on `Array.isArray(value)` alone.

⚠️ Also decide where the refusal belongs. Throwing from `viewFilterRuleToNode` means a saved view with one bad rule throws at render rather than returning a narrower result — that may be right, but it is a different blast radius from a hand-authored filter, and a stored rule was authored long ago by someone who is not present. Say which you chose and why.

## Related

objectui#8530 / PR #8551 (the object arm, landed; where this was measured) · objectui#8514 / PR #8529 (the matcher-side sibling) · objectui#3431 (the earlier defect in this same stored-view path, whose fix this function is)
